# ethereum-optimism/op-geth Monthly Report (February 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
In February 2026, development on `op-geth` focused on refining the infrastructure for the Superchain ecosystem, with a particular emphasis on synchronization stability and interoperability. Key efforts included transitioning to more robust tooling for Superchain scripts and addressing critical architectural questions regarding safe label management within the `op-supernode`. The team also prioritized resolving synchronization bugs and improving the developer experience by investigating edge cases in the ETH bridge tutorial and initial Execution Layer (EL) sync processes.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### Tooling & Dependency Management
Efforts were made to modernize and stabilize the scripts used for Superchain operations.
*   **Superchain Sync Improvements:** The `sync-superchain.sh` script was updated to replace `dasel` with `yq` for reading TOML files, favoring a more stable and widely adopted tool ([#762](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/pull/762)). This followed a brief exploration of adding compatibility for `dasel` v3 ([#761](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/pull/761)).
*   **Internal Updates:** The project updated its `fork.yaml` reference to `v1.16.8` to maintain alignment with the latest internal specifications ([#760](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/pull/760)).

### Protocol & Feature Support
*   **Flashblocks & Tracing:** Discussions progressed regarding the integration of Firehose Live Tracer and Flashblocks support directly into the main `op-geth` repository. This move aims to reduce the operational complexity and high disk space requirements currently associated with running archive versions of Reth for these features ([#756](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/756)).

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### Closed Issues
*   **L1 Polling Fix:** A bug in `op-supernode` where HTTP L1 URLs inadvertently disabled L1 polling—preventing virtual nodes from receiving head updates—was successfully resolved ([#19012](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/19012)).

### New & Active Issues
*   **Supernode Architecture:** Significant discussion is ongoing regarding how `op-supernode` handles safe labels. The community is weighing whether the Consensus Layer (CL) should remain the sole controller of the engine to prevent stateful controllers from falling out of sync, versus the potential architectural trade-offs of making the `op-node` interop-aware ([#18976](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/18976)).
*   **EL Sync Correctness:** Developers are addressing a "buggy" behavior where the `op-node` marks a target as finalized immediately after an initial EL Sync. Proposed solutions include running derivation from a prior L1 block to verify alignment with the snap-synced chain ([#17631](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/17631)).
*   **Interoperability Testing:** The `TestInteropReadiness` test was reopened as a priority. It remains skipped pending support for explicit output roots in the super DG ([#18616](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/18616)).
*   **SuperRoots for Unsafe Data:** A new discussion was initiated regarding whether `op-supernode` should return "SuperRoots" for unsafe data at specific timestamps, even when verified data is not yet available ([#19059](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/19059)).

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
The month's activity highlights a strong focus on the developer experience and cross-project compatibility. Collaboration was evident in the technical deep-dive into the `BlockNotFoundError` reported in the ETH bridge tutorial. This investigation revealed a discrepancy between the Optimism SDK's validation logic and viem's withdrawal guides, leading to a community-driven effort to ensure state roots are properly published before users attempt to prove withdrawals ([#1956](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/1956)). Additionally, the shift from `dasel` to `yq` reflects a responsive maintenance team that prioritizes contributor feedback regarding environment compatibility.
